blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A generator seeds one random.Random with an integer, then picks each project's region with draw.choice(REGIONS) and its cost with draw.randint(100, 900). A test pins the hash of its output. With no change to the generator's code, what can make that test fail?

options.text: Running it in a new process, since each process seeds the stream anew
options.says: Seeding anew with the same seed gives the same stream; GridCap large's hash matched in fresh interpreters.

options.text: A newer Python, since only random() is promised to repeat across versions
options.says: Right: Python guarantees the sequence of random(), not the algorithms of choice or randint.

options.text: A new PYTHONHASHSEED, since random.Random hashes the seed it is given
options.says: An integer seed does not go through string hashing: two different PYTHONHASHSEED values gave the same portfolio.

options.text: Nothing, since a fixed seed fixes every method's output for all time
options.says: Python's documentation promises that only for random(); the helpers built on it may change between versions.

origin.section: The Same Seed Gives the Same Portfolio, in This Process and in a Fresh One

questions.stem: A generator draws each project's kind, cost and start, in that order, from one shared stream. Version 2 draws a crew size for every project, right after its cost. Which values that version 1 already produced change?

options.text: None, since the new draw fills only the new crew-size field
options.says: The new draw takes a number from the shared stream, so every later draw gets a different one.

options.text: Only the crew sizes, since kind, cost and start are drawn as before
options.says: Crew size did not exist in version 1; and the start, drawn after it, now gets another number.

options.text: The first start and every later value, since each draw shifts the rest
options.says: Right: the first project's kind and cost come before the new draw; every draw after it moves along the stream.

options.text: Only the last project, since new draws are taken from the stream's end
options.says: Draws are taken in order from the front; in streams.py every project after the first new draw changed.

origin.section: One Shared Stream Ties Every Draw to Every Draw Before It

questions.stem: A generator's tests check all of its invariants on the default seed, and they pass. A colleague adds a test that checks them at twenty other seeds. What does the new test add?

options.text: Evidence about other portfolios, since one seed checks only one portfolio
options.says: Right: an invariant is a claim about every seed, and each seed is a different portfolio.

options.text: Nothing, since the same code builds every portfolio in the same way
options.says: The same code with other draws makes other portfolios; gridcap's own tests never checked large or other seeds.

options.text: A flaky test, since another seed gives other output on every run
options.says: Each seed gives the same portfolio on every run, so a test at twenty seeds is as repeatable as one at one seed.

options.text: Nothing, since a planted violation has already shown the checks work
options.says: A plant shows that a check can fail, not that other seeds pass it; only the checks at other seeds show that.

origin.section: Invariants State What Every Portfolio Must Satisfy, and a Test Checks Them at Many Seeds
